segments.text: Why does a thirty-five dollar aluminum pot from 1933 out-brew a three thousand dollar espresso machine?
segments.title: THE $3,000 PARADOX

segments.text: In 1933, Alfonso Bialetti watched his wife wash laundry with a boiler that forced hot water up a pipe. He took that exact physics to build the Moka Express.
segments.title: THE LAUNDRY BOILER

segments.text: Zero electric pumps. Expanding steam generates 1.5 bars of vapor pressure, driving hot water through the coffee basket at 95 degrees.
segments.title: 1.5 BARS OF STEAM

segments.text: Its octagonal aluminum body diffuses heat ten times faster than steel, while coffee oils create a protective patina. That is why Italians ban dish soap.
segments.title: THE 8-SIDED SHIELD

segments.text: Zero circuit boards to fry, zero plastic pods, and twenty-five years of daily coffee for less than half a cent per cup.
segments.title: HEIRLOOM LIFESPAN

segments.text: The Bialetti Moka Express scores 9.1 out of 10 on the Special Index: A True Gem.
segments.title: THE SPECIAL VERDICT
